job.style: a passage that starts from a common wrong idea and corrects it

passage: Many people believe that eating only one type of 'superfood' is enough to stay healthy, but this is a dangerous myth. A truly balanced diet requires a variety of food groups to provide all necessary nutrients. For instance, some think that roughage or fibre is useless because our bodies cannot digest it, but fibre is actually essential for smooth digestion and bowel health. Another common mistake is thinking that only oily snacks cause weight gain, while extra portions of rice or roti are harmless. In reality, the body converts any excess energy from carbohydrates into stored fat. Furthermore, many people mistakenly believe that white polished rice or maida are superior because they look cleaner and finer than whole grains. In truth, whole grains like millets and brown rice are far more nutritious as they retain the bran and germ. Finally, some assume that vegetarians cannot get enough protein without meat or eggs. This is incorrect, as pulses, legumes, and dairy are excellent plant-based protein sources that can easily meet our daily requirements. A balanced plate must include a mix of these diverse foods, tailored to your specific age and activity level, rather than following a one-size-fits-all approach.

items.evidence: For instance, some think that roughage or fibre is useless because our bodies cannot digest it, but fibre is actually essential for smooth digestion and bowel health.
items.q: Meena peels all her fruit and eats only maida bread to avoid fibre. What will most likely happen?
options: Her bowels will not work as smoothly
Nothing, since the body cannot use fibre anyway
She will stay healthier, as refined food is cleaner
She will lose energy, since fibre fuels the body
items.explain: Fibre cannot be digested, but it is essential for smooth digestion and bowel health, so avoiding it causes problems.

wrong.why: thinks refined, finer food is healthier
confuses fibre with an energy-giving nutrient

items.evidence: In reality, the body converts any excess energy from carbohydrates into stored fat.
items.q: Raju avoids oily snacks but eats four extra rotis every day. What will most likely happen?
options: He will gain weight from the extra carbohydrates
He will not gain weight, as rotis have no oil
He will stay fit because roti is healthy food
He will lose weight by skipping oily snacks
items.explain: The body turns any extra energy from carbohydrates like roti into stored fat, so Raju will gain weight.

wrong.why: thinks only oily food causes weight gain
thinks plenty of one healthy food is always fine
over-generalises that skipping oil alone means weight loss

items.evidence: In truth, whole grains like millets and brown rice are far more nutritious as they retain the bran and germ.
items.q: A mother switches from maida to whole wheat atta and millets. Which explains why this is healthier?
options: These grains keep their bran and germ
These grains look cleaner and finer than maida
Millets are cheaper, so families can eat more
These grains give energy, so no vegetables are needed
items.explain: Whole grains like millets are more nutritious because they keep the bran and germ, which maida loses.

wrong.why: links looking clean and fine with being healthy
sees millets only as cheap grains, not nutritious ones
thinks one good food replaces other food groups

items.evidence: This is incorrect, as pulses, legumes, and dairy are excellent plant-based protein sources that can easily meet our daily requirements.
items.q: Anita is a vegetarian who eats no eggs. How can she get enough protein each day?
options: By eating dal, beans, milk and paneer
She cannot; protein comes only from meat or eggs
By taking a vitamin tablet with her meals
By eating plenty of potatoes and green leaves
items.explain: Pulses, legumes and dairy are excellent protein sources that can easily meet a vegetarian's daily needs.

wrong.why: thinks vegetarians cannot get enough protein
thinks a vitamin tablet can replace food nutrients
thinks potatoes count like other healthy vegetables
